claims.text: The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy is homogeneous.
Temperature-dependent short-range order is the main cause of the unusual stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range order enhances local lattice distortions.
Short-range-order-induced lattice distortions affect dislocation mobility.
Short-range order affects creep and hardening through its effect on dislocation mobility.
Short-range order changes thermal expansion by creating internal mismatch stresses.
Aging HfNbTaTiZr at approximately 700 °C for one hour promotes short-range-order development.
The local lattice distortions associated with aging-induced short-range order inhibit dislocation motion.
Inhibition of dislocation motion by short-range order increases hardness.
Inhibition of dislocation motion by short-range order increases creep resistance.
Internal stresses arising from mismatched local lattice strains alter the intrinsic elastic response and thermal expansion behavior.
Relative to as-cast HfNbTaTiZr, material aged at 700 °C will have increased microhardness.
Relative to as-cast HfNbTaTiZr, material aged at 700 °C will have a lower creep rate at 1250 °C.
Relative to as-cast HfNbTaTiZr, material aged at 700 °C will exhibit a modified elastic modulus over the tested temperature range.
Relative to as-cast HfNbTaTiZr, material aged at 700 °C will exhibit a modified thermal expansion coefficient over the tested temperature range.
A reversible annealing treatment can disrupt the short-range order produced by aging.
Disrupting short-range order should reverse the aging-induced mechanical and thermoelastic differences.
